cli.short.scope_activate: Activate the desired Managed Scope policy through preview and apply
cli.long.scope_activate: Activate the current desired policy with an empty Candidate Set through the existing Scope Change preview/apply flow. This command does not edit rules or author Entries. Safe automatic changes apply immediately; changes requiring human approval stop without a prompt and retain a preview under .aoci/scope-change/. Run the printed approve and apply commands, replacing <id> with your reviewer identity. --json returns the existing Scope Change result on success; an approval stop returns exit 2 with preview_file, approve_command and apply_command in error details. Legacy source drift and other governance refusals remain unchanged.

check.detail: Details: disk %d / Entries %d | RawMissing %d, ActionableMissing %d (IncludedMissing %d), CurationExcludedMissing %d, SkippedMissing %d (PendingCurationMissing %d), StaleCurationDecisions %d, Orphan %d, Stale %d, Unbaselined %d, LineEndingOnly %d | S quota %d, E scale %d, tagparse %d (Warnings do not block) | Agent ready %v | index about %d tokens
check.hint_escale: Note: inspect E scale details with aoci index score --dim escale.
check.hint_excluded: Note: %d Curation-excluded path(s) are CurationExcludedMissing, a completed exclude decision. RawMissing preserves the physical fact but does not block a commit.
check.hint_included: Note: %d Included path(s) are IncludedMissing, an ActionableMissing subset that still needs an Entry.
check.hint_line_endings: Note: %d LineEndingOnly paths represent CRLF/LF differences only; they are not Stale and do not block a commit.
check.hint_orphan: Note: see aoci verify for complete Orphan paths and cleanup guidance.
check.hint_pending: Note: %d paths are PendingCurationMissing and also %d Pending members of SkippedMissing; unresolved include/exclude semantics block a commit.
check.hint_skipped: Note: %d non-Pending SkippedMissing path(s), currently mainly unreadable technical skips, do not block a commit; see verify --json for reasons.
check.hint_squota: Note: inspect S quota details with aoci index score --dim squota.
check.s_coverage: S coverage: C%d+ Entries %d/%d have S (%d%% absent) | by band: %s
check.hint_s_coverage: Note: %d%% of C%d+ Entries carry S:- (hint threshold %d%%). Run aoci_maintain with intent=cognition_optimization so a model reviews those Entries; this is a hint, not a gate.
check.e_scale: E scale: %d of %d Code Entries carry a scale letter the source line count contradicts
check.hint_e_scale: Note: a file growing across a band is ordinary. The letter is corrected on the Entry's next drift, or now through aoci_maintain with intent=cognition_optimization, which ranks these Entries for review.
check.hint_stale_curation: Note: stale Curation decisions expired automatically after source_sha256 changed. Their paths re-entered ActionableMissing or PendingCurationMissing and do not add a second Issue.
check.hint_tagparse: Note: inspect unparseable tags with aoci index score --dim tagparse.
check.issue_cognition_budget: Cognition budget enforcement failed: Whole-Index %d exceeds max %d or %d field limits are violated
check.issue_dict: %d dictionary violation(s) → inspect aoci index score --dim dict, then repair Entries or extend the dictionary
check.issue_entries: Entries governance: ActionableMissing %d, Stale %d → this Legacy layout is read-only since 0.2.0; migrate with aoci cognition onboard start --json, then let the host Agent run the Guide; see aoci verify for RawMissing, IncludedMissing, and Curation subsets
check.issue_format: %d format error(s) → inspect aoci index score --dim format and repair them
check.issue_locale_migration: Locale migration %s → %s still has %d unresolved managed surface category(ies) → follow aoci index agent guide; Check cannot pass before the receipt is complete
check.issue_observed_review: %d observe evidence changes require explicit review and acknowledgement
check.issue_pending: %d PendingCurationMissing path(s) → run aoci index agent guide and complete Curation Stage, Diff, and Apply before checking again
check.issue_scope_change: Managed Scope policy changed and requires an explicit Scope Change (desired %s, active %s)
check.issue_unbaselined: %d Unbaselined path(s) → run aoci index agent guide for the safe action; do not use scan --force directly

guide.volumes_instruction_maintain: For ordinary Volumes v1 maintenance, call no-argument aoci_maintain in the current MCP session and submit its complete candidate/batch through aoci_update_entry. For Code, code_batch_id must equal code_plan.batch_id and every Code candidate.batch_id; authoring_batch.batch_identity is not valid there. If an applied batch reports remaining nonzero, call aoci_maintain again against the new preimage and do not run terminal proof yet. After the final successful formal-write batch reports remaining=0, run commands.verify, commands.check (the aggregate Check), and commands.guide in that order; do not call Maintain or write again, and report only their actual returned results. Do not run the Legacy-only aoci index agent plan command.

guide.volumes_instruction_scope_change: The desired Managed Scope policy or budget differs from the active Baseline receipt, so authoring is blocked. Run the scope_activate command to apply safe changes. If human approval is required, activation stops without writing and returns a preview plus approve and apply commands; follow those commands with a real reviewer. Use S only when the constraint cannot be inferred from F/R/A and affects system understanding or modification. Keep S:- when no qualifying constraint exists; for a C7-C9 object that S:- asserts you looked there and found nothing a modifier could get wrong, and an S:- written without that look is as wrong as an invented S. volumes.authoring.database.contract: Database authoring contract: use %s and current dictionary %s. Under the official starter dictionary only, G means genuinely cross-domain and Z means sufficient evidence was understood but no named category fits; insufficient evidence is not Z and must be reported. Classification or dictionary gaps never enter S. Custom formal Meta meanings remain authoritative. FRAS v2 limits are F<=%d runes, R<=%d runes/%d items, A<=%d runes/%d items. S admits only non-inferable, error-preventing facts and uses %s. For C6-C9 tables, before settling on S:- look for evidence-backed S constraints where the behaviour is actually decided: the DDL's keys, checks, triggers, and cascades, and the application code that writes the table, including soft-delete, uniqueness, and ordering rules. Use S only when the constraint cannot be inferred from F/R/A and affects system understanding or modification. Keep S:- when no qualifying constraint exists; for a C7-C9 table that S:- asserts you looked there and found nothing a modifier could get wrong. R accepts exact managed identities such as %s or %s, separates multiple identities with %q, and uses %q for no strong relation. Dotted tags and bare relation names are read compatibility only and must not be authored. The example calibrates field separation only; do not copy its semantics.
volumes.authoring.database.example: users[%s]: F:Stores user account records | R:- | A:user_id | S:Hard deletion is forbidden because retained ownership history depends on stable account identifiers
volumes.authoring.meta: Read authoring_meta before authoring any affected Volume candidate. It is the exact formal aoci.meta.txt bytes returned by aoci_header; runtime instructions complete compatibility contracts without changing or substituting those bytes.
volumes.authoring.transport: Author every candidate directly as aoci_update_entry arguments; the batch is sized to fit one inline call, so no staging files or scripts are needed. First read every candidate's source, in parallel where the host allows, and read a large file's structure and the parts that decide its behaviour rather than every line; then submit the whole batch in one call. R and S have token ceilings as well as rune quotas: see governance.budget, a token is UTF-8 bytes/3, so one CJK character is one token. If context is lost mid-batch, call aoci_maintain again: the unchanged repository reproduces the same batch and candidate identities. Batches are not user decisions: after a successful write, call aoci_maintain again at once and keep going until remaining is 0 without asking the user to continue.
volumes.optimization.review: A candidate whose selection_reason is s_absent_high_importance is a C7-C9 Entry with S:-. Look at where its behaviour is decided, then either author the constraint or resubmit the Entry unchanged; an unchanged batch is a valid optimization result.
cli.short.ui: Serve a local, read-only status page for one or more repositories
cli.long.ui:
Start a loopback-only HTTP page that shows the cognition index of one or more
repositories: identity, index header, Code and Database Volumes, budget, chunk
plan, governance drift, running aoci mcp servers, host integrations, and the
next step the Guide recommends. It reads the same facts Verify, Check, Guide,
and Maintain consume, takes no lock, writes nothing, and is not an MCP
transport. Repositories come from --repo, --also, and (on Linux) the running
aoci mcp processes of the current user.

--detach starts the page in the background, detached from this shell, and prints
only its URL; a page already running for this repository is reused when this version started it; a page from an older binary must be stopped first. --stop ends it.
